root_cause.text: In `drm/xe` exec queue initialization (`__xe_exec_queue_init()`), the error path freed partially created LRCs but did not call the queue’s `fini` routine to release the allocated GuC ID / remove the queue from the GuC list, leaving a damaged `xe_exec_queue` entry behind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says “Every call to queue init should have a corresponding fini call” and “Skipping this would mean skipping removal of the queue from GuC list (which is part of guc_id allocation),” then changes the `err_lrc` path from only `xe_lrc_put(q->lrc[i])` to `__xe_exec_queue_fini(q)`, and makes `xe_lrc_put()` tolerate NULL so fini can run before LRCs are freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add exec queue finalization logic to release queue-specific resources and LRC references during teardown.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `__xe_exec_queue_fini(struct xe_exec_queue *q)` was added. It calls `q->ops->fini(q)` and then iterates from `i = 0` to `i < q->width`, calling `xe_lrc_put(q->lrc[i])` for each LRC entry.
intent_record.how: This adds a centralized teardown path for exec queues that first performs queue-specific finalization and then releases all per-width LRC references, ensuring resources are properly cleaned up when an exec queue is destroyed or unwound.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate exec queue initialization failure cleanup by reusing the common fini path instead of manually releasing partially initialized resources.
intent_record.what: In the error path of __xe_exec_queue_init(), the code no longer manually decrements through already-initialized LRC objects with a for loop and xe_lrc_put(); instead it now calls __xe_exec_queue_fini(q). At the same time, the static definition of __xe_exec_queue_fini() shown in the hunk is removed from this location, including its q->ops->fini(q) call and the loop that releases all q->lrc entries.
intent_record.how: The initialization failure cleanup now delegates to the shared fini helper rather than duplicating partial teardown logic. This centralizes resource release for exec queue initialization failures and reduces the risk of inconsistent cleanup behavior between error handling and normal destruction.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL check to xe_lrc_put() so releasing a missing lrc becomes a no-op instead of causing a fault.
intent_record.what: The function xe_lrc_put() was changed to add a null check: it now calls kref_put(&lrc->refcount, xe_lrc_destroy) only when lrc is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, passing a NULL pointer to xe_lrc_put() will no longer dereference it and trigger a crash; the function now safely does nothing in that case.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the post-init cleanup split and the new unified free path, so the specific bug root cause is not present here. The vulnerable construct described was an init error path that freed partial LRCs but did not call the queue fini routine to release the GuC ID / remove the queue from the GuC list. In this snippet, `__xe_exec_queue_init()` only performs LRC setup and on failure does `for (i = i - 1; i >= 0; --i) xe_lrc_finish(q->lrc + i); return err;`, while the outer creator handles failure with `goto err_post_alloc; __xe_exec_queue_free(q); return ERR_PTR(err);`. Also, the final teardown path was centralized: `xe_exec_queue_fini()` now calls `__xe_exec_queue_free(q)` after `xe_lrc_finish(...)` and `xe_device_mem_access_put(...)`. Since the buggy omission in the root cause is about the error path not invoking fini / not releasing the exec queue state, and this diff shows a dedicated cleanup path introduced for alloc/init separation rather than that missing release logic, the vulnerable construct is absent in this commit version and the fix is effectively present in the cleanup structure shown.
